column1: # ADR-0056 D9 / V16: the shared case table of the canonical bundle digest. Every
# implementation of the digest runs it: Go (internal/edition, bundle_digest_test.go)
# and deploy-user.sh (A5c). This table is plain ASCII, TAB-separated, no quoting; the
# case files are not always (content-utf8 holds a word in UTF-8 and is hashed as bytes).
# A row is   case<TAB>digest<TAB>input   (the third column is absent for `empty`: its
# input is no bytes at all, and its row has two columns).
#   case    the name of the directory beside this file that holds the bundle: its
#           files, flat, named as in the B2 grammar. A case with no directory is the
#           empty bundle, and `empty` is the only one (git holds no empty directory).
#   input   the exact bytes the digest is the sha256 of, spelled for printf: \x00 is
#           NUL and \n is LF, nothing else is escaped. The bytes are, for the files in
#           byte order of their names,  name NUL hex(sha256(content)) LF  one after
#           another (D9). An implementation derives them from the directory and
#           compares the sha256 with the digest column; it need not read this column.
#   digest  lower-case hex of the sha256 of those bytes.
# Anyone can check a row with no program of ours:
#   printf '<input column>' | shasum -a 256        (the digest column is the hash)
#   printf '<content of the file>' | shasum -a 256 (the hex inside the input column)
# The input holds no percent sign, so the column is a safe printf format as it stands.
# The cases that differ by one byte from another case (the name: file-name-differs;
# the content: content-differs, content-newline; the pairing of names and contents:
# two-files-swapped) must all have different digests. byte-order puts four names whose
# order is not the one a locale-aware sort gives (a-b, a.b, a0, ab: byte order is
# 0x2d, 0x2e, 0x30, 0x62 after `a`), so a shell must sort with LC_ALL=C.
